---
title: "Journeys through this playbook"
description: "The same work seen from four roles: where each one goes, in what order, and what each stop leaves behind."
---

There is no need to read the playbook front to back. Each journey below sets out the order the
pages come up for one role: the analyst, the commissioner, the critical friend or the Analysis
Senior Responsible Officer.

**Each journey follows one piece of work.** You come to the playbook through a single output, and
leave it when that output is signed off.

**Each journey is a table, to work down.** Alongside it, the role's own page sets out what that
role is responsible for in each phase.

Every journey table has the same four columns: where you are, where to read it, what you do there,
and what you leave behind. The last column read on its own is the evidence trail for one piece of
analysis. There is a **Done** box beside it, so in print or in the Word copy the table works as a
checklist.

## Where each journey is

Each journey now sits on the page for the role it belongs to, with the rest of what that role is
accountable for around it.

| Your role on this piece of work | Your journey |
|---|---|
| You are doing the analysis | [The analyst](../06-roles/analyst.qmd) |
| You are reviewing somebody else's analysis | [The critical friend](../06-roles/critical-friend.qmd) |
| You asked for the analysis | [The commissioner](../06-roles/commissioner.qmd) |
| You are accountable for a Business Critical output | [The Analysis Senior Responsible Officer](../06-roles/analysis-senior-responsible-officer.qmd) |

## One piece of work, four roles

NHSBSA's decision sheet gives **a funding allocation formula** as an example of Level 4 BCA work.
Here is that example through all four roles, so the journeys above can be read against one piece of
work.

This is the route the playbook sets out for work of that kind. It is not a record of any particular
piece of work.

### Commissioner

- State the decision the formula informs, the deadline, and how certain the answer has to be.
  [Phase 1, engagement and scoping](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd).
- Score the six impact dimensions with the analyst.
  [Deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd).
- The Finance row scores 4 for analysis that "determines, or is relied on for, major funding,
  investment, commissioning, resource-allocation or policy decisions". A funding allocation formula
  is that, so one dimension at 4 settles it: the work is Business Critical, at Level 4.
- Say so at scoping, before the design.
- Find the time and resource Level 4 assurance needs, or agree a narrower question.

### Analyst

- Agree the question, and record the scope, the boundaries and the assumptions.
  [Phase 1, engagement and scoping](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd).
- Choose the method, and place it among the eight model types.
  [Phase 2, design](../02-design/index.qmd).
- Do your own verification and validation first.
- Log decisions as you make them.
- Quantify the uncertainty, and say what rests on which assumption.
  [Uncertainty, assumptions and limitations](../09-resources/r10-uncertainty.qmd).

### Critical friend

- At Level 4 you are a Lead Assurer from outside the delivering team, and external review applies
  as well. [How independent you have to be](../06-roles/critical-friend.qmd#how-independent-you-have-to-be).
- You are named at design.
- Reproduce the calculations from source.
- Read the documentation as a document, not only the numbers.
- Examine the structural and conceptual assumptions, and report what you find back.

### Analysis Senior Responsible Officer

- You are named at scoping, and the register entry is made then.
  [Business Critical analysis](../08-business-critical/index.qmd).
- Confirm design governance has been followed before the analysis starts.
- Review the assurance evidence, and approve the formula as fit for its intended use, after the
  Lead Assurer has signed off.
- Revalidate the designation annually, and before any reuse for a new purpose.
  [Phase 5, review](../05-review/index.qmd).

**Four jobs, and between them seven sections.** That is the whole of what a Level 4 piece of work
asks of this playbook, and Level 1 work asks a great deal less: one analyst, a colleague within
the team, and [deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd).
